Subject: Marketplace listing copy & SLA -- two quick clarifications

Hi Markus,

Thanks for submitting the listing draft for Redwood Inference to the Azure Marketplace. Two quick clarifications from our side before we can move to co-sell enablement:

1) Support SLA wording: our policy requires that public listing text avoid absolute uptime guarantees unless backed by a publicly visible SLA doc. Your copy currently says "99.9% uptime SLA for production deployments." Can you confirm whether that is a marketing statement or a contractual claim supported by the SLA matrix? If contractual, we need a link to the SLA doc.

2) Branding/claim language: the line "Redwood delivers enterprise-grade, low-latency inference under $0.01/token" is flagged by our team because we disallow explicit price-to-quality claims that could be interpreted as a guarantee. Please revise to a less prescriptive phrase or provide substantiation.

Attach: an internal review checklist for marketplace claims is attached.

Appreciate a quick reply — the co-sell team is gating the phrase-level review.

Best,
Azure Marketplace Compliance Team
Azure Marketplace Operations

Hi Azure team — thanks for the flags and quick read. Short answers and next steps below.

1) SLA phrasing: The 99.9% figure is part of our Dedicated offering contract (reserved capacity customers) but it is not a universal guarantee across all hosted plans. We should not present it as a blanket public guarantee on the marketplace listing. We'll change the public listing to: "SLA-backed performance options for Dedicated deployments; contact us for details." We'll attach the SLA matrix and legal-approved phrasing for your review.

2) Pricing claim: the $0.01/token line is an illustrative unit-economics example from our pricing page, not a promise. We'll replace it with: "Cost-effective inference optimized for production workloads (contact sales for customized pricing)."

Attaching an updated draft (v3) and the SLA matrix. Vanessa, can you and Lauren confirm the wording below is fine to push? Karthik, please loop legal if you want different guardrails.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
